title: KS-1516: What may an unverified opentimestamps/blockchain timestamp claim?
bluf: Today, creating an opentimestamps or blockchain timestamp answers verified:true and stores verified=true, though both proofs are generated locally (placeholders). /api/timestamps/verify also returns verified:true for a forged opentimestamps proof with no stored row. KS-1404 closed this forgery path for rfc3161 only. It is a mock reported as verified on an evidentiary path, filed P2. Any choice changes the live API's answers (production change once built). Fixing already-stored rows is a separate approval of yours and not decided here.

sources.quote: creating an opentimestamps or blockchain timestamp answers verified: true and persists verified = true
with no stored row returns verified: true from /verify
KS-1404 closed this same forgery path for rfc3161 only

options.label: Report verified:false for both types until a real check exists (changes live API)
options.detail: Agent build. Honest and simplest. Existing clients see verified:false for these types.

options.label: Require a stored row and honour its verified column (agent build; changes live API)
options.detail: Rfc3161 shape. Closes the forgery path; creation still stores verified=true unless also changed.

options.label: Stop advertising the two types in supportedTypes (changes live API)
options.detail: Agent build. Removes the claim entirely; clients using the types would be affected.

default_action: After 48 h nothing is built and nothing changes (the safest reversible state; the false claim stays live meanwhile). The ticket stays parked for your ruling.
